messages.text:
Dear Priya,

Thank you for reaching out, and we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. We understand how disappointing it must be to receive a damaged item, especially one intended as a gift. Please rest assured that we take this matter seriously. Could you please provide your order number and a photo of the damaged mug so we can resolve this as quickly as possible?

Best regards,
[YOUR NAME]

cards.title: The brief
cards.text: Reply to this customer email. What happened: 1 of 2 mugs arrived broken, it's a gift for Saturday. What we're doing: replacement sent today by express, arrives Friday, no need to return the broken one. Tone: warm, human, no corporate phrases. Under 70 words. Sign off as [NAME]. Email: [PASTE]

slides.note: Remove order numbers, addresses and email addresses before pasting.

messages.text:
Hi Priya,

I'm so sorry, that's not how a gift should arrive. I've sent a replacement mug today by express, so it'll be with you by Friday, in time for Saturday. No need to send the broken one back, just wrap it up and recycle it carefully.

Thanks for letting me know.
[NAME]

caption:
How to reply to a customer complaint with AI: vague prompt vs specific prompt

Same complaint (an example pottery shop, invented): one mug arrived smashed, and it was a birthday gift for Saturday.

Prompt A: "Reply to this complaint: [PASTE EMAIL]"
Polite and formal, and it asked the customer for a photo and an order number. More waiting.

Prompt B: "Reply to this customer email. What happened: 1 of 2 mugs arrived broken, it's a gift for Saturday. What we're doing: replacement sent today by express, arrives Friday, no need to return the broken one. Tone: warm, human, no corporate phrases. Under 70 words. Sign off as [NAME]. Email: [PASTE]"
Warm and short: sorry, replacement on its way, arrives Friday, keep the broken one.

A wasn't wrong. It just didn't know what you can offer. Decide the fix first.

Remove order numbers, addresses and emails before pasting.
